articles.title: Observing Near Home
articles.summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide for amateur astronomers seeking to make the most of observing from near-home locations, even with light pollution. It recommends numerous resources, including specific star atlases, observing guides, and online lists, for identifying double stars, deep-sky objects, planets, and the Moon. The author highlights the value of regular, accessible observing sessions for skill development and exploring a wide range of celestial objects, balancing them with less frequent trips to dark-sky sites.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This article discusses the lunar crater named Omar Khayyam, highlighting a specific libration event that offers a rare viewing opportunity for its details. It delves into the true legacy of Omar Khayyam, revealing him as a prominent mathematician and astronomer of his time, famous for work on cubic equations, astronomical tables, and calendar reform, rather than solely for his poetry. The piece encourages readers to appreciate the scientific contributions behind the name.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky Challenge and Column
articles.summary: Akkana Peck's 'Shallow Sky Challenge' article aims to debunk the misconception that solar system observing is less challenging than deep-sky astronomy. It proposes several difficult targets for April observers, including the distant centaur object Chiron and moons orbiting asteroids like Ida (Dactyl) and Eugenia. The author encourages amateur astronomers to attempt these observations and demonstrate the complexity of shallow sky viewing to their deep-sky counterparts.

articles.title: Auction XXI
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its annual astronomical auction and swap meet, Auction XXI, on Sunday, April 8, 2001, at Houge Park in San Jose. This event serves as the organization's sole fundraiser, with a 10% commission on sales, which is tax-deductible as SJAA is a 501(c)(3) educational organization. This year's event features two changes: it will be held on a Sunday to avoid scheduling conflicts, and the auction will precede the swap meet.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series
articles.summary: The Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series announced an event on April 11, 2001, featuring Dr. Gregory Laughlin of NASA Ames Research Center. The non-technical program, titled 'The Long-term Future of the Sun, the Earth, and the Solar System,' will discuss the ultimate fate of our planet over billions of years. The free lecture will be held at Smithwick Theater, Foothill College, and is open to the public.

articles.title: New Board of Directors and Officers
articles.summary: At the general meeting on February 10, a new Board of Directors was elected to serve 2-year terms, welcoming new members like Paul Mancuso and Bob Havner, while thanking Akkana Peck and Dave North for their service. Subsequently, on March 10, the newly constituted Board elected its officers for one-year terms, with Mike Koop as President, Bob Havner as Vice-President, Jim Van Nuland as Secretary, and Gary Mitchell as Treasurer.

articles.title: Be a Visiting Astronomer in Bay Area Schools
articles.summary: Project ASTRO is recruiting amateur and professional astronomers to partner with Bay Area teachers for the 2001-2002 school year, teaching astronomy to 4th-9th grade students. Volunteers will attend a free summer training workshop and commit to at least four classroom visits throughout the school year. Applications are due April 27, 2001, for this rewarding educational outreach program.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The SJAA Loaner Scope program offers various telescopes to its members, with the article detailing the current status of available scopes, those currently on loan with due dates, and scopes with extended loan periods. Members can contact Mike Koop to borrow equipment or be added to a waiting list for popular items. The program provides a diverse range of instruments, from refractors and Newtonians to specialized solar scopes and spectroscopes.
